identity.name: Duchy of Massa and Carrara

land.text: the Duchy of Massa and the Principality of Carrara, 'annexed by her son and heir to the Duchy of Modena and Reggio' on Maria Beatrice's death in 1829

successors.note: Infobox: Francis IV annexes the territories on 14 November 1836; 'it was legally transformed into a district of the duchy only in 1836'; 'Many authors argue that the final year of the states of Massa and Carrara was 1829'.

land.text: assigned to the Principality of Lucca and Piombino in 1806

successors.note: Infobox successor for the French interlude 1806-1814, after which the duchy was restored.

land.text: incorporated into the Cispadane Republic in 1796, which 'later became the Cisalpine Republic'

successors.note: Infobox successor for the interlude 1796-1814; the cispadane-republic dossier lists this duchy as a predecessor and records no territory event.

capitals.name: Massa
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Massa Carrara'; Massa is the seat of the Cybo-Malaspina court. Carrara is the second town.

capitals.name: Massa
capitals.note: After the French rule of 10 May 1796 to 30 May 1814.

correction.text: the Lordship (later marquisate, principality and duchy) of Massa and Carrara

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria shape. The page gives no area. Two 10 km circles around Massa and Carrara (about two 253 km2 cells) stand for it, the same drawing the duchy-of-modena-and-reggio dossier uses for 1829. The province of Massa-Carrara, which includes Lunigiana, is larger than the duchy and is not used.

correction.text: the restored duchy: 'The Congress again assigned to Maria Beatrice the ancestral duchy'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe after the French years 1796-1814. The Lunigiana fiefs held in 1815 are in the ledger only (January to December 1815).

region.text: the Lordship of Massa with the Lordship of Carrara

ledger.note: 22 February 1473: the Malaspina buy the Lordship of Carrara. The state's original nucleus 'officially born on 22 February 1473 with the purchase of the Lordship of Carrara'; Giacomo I Malaspina ruled 1473-1481. The page does not say who sold Carrara; the infobox 'Established' is 22 February 1664, the date the duchy was created.

1520: Ricciarda Malaspina marries Lorenzo Cybo, and the Cybo-Malaspina line begins ('married in 1520 with Lorenzo Cybo'; in 1529 she obtained investiture of the marquisate from Charles V). Same state, same colour.

1568: Alberico I becomes Prince of Massa and Marquis of Carrara (ruler list: 'from 1568'). The page's text says Massa and Carrara were 'elevated respectively to marquisate and to principality', which contradicts the ruler list on which title belongs to which town.
22 February 1664: the Principality of Massa becomes a duchy. Leopold I of Habsburg 'raised the Principality of Massa to the rank of duchy' under Alberico II; infobox 'Established: 22 February 1664'.

region.text: the duchy, taken by Napoleon's troops and incorporated into the Cispadane Republic

ledger.note: 1796: the French take Massa and Carrara. 'In 1796 the Este were deprived of their possessions by the troops of Napoleon', who 'incorporated the territory into the Cispadane Republic, which later became the Cisalpine Republic'; infobox 'French rule: 10 May 1796-30 May 1814'. The page gives no month for the incorporation; the Cispadane Republic dossier begins in October 1796 and records no event for this land.

region.text: the Duchy of Massa and Carrara, assigned to the Principality of Lucca and Piombino

ledger.note: 1806: Napoleon gives the duchy to Elisa's principality. 'in 1806, the French emperor assigned the Duchy of Massa and Carrara to the Principality of Lucca and Piombino'. The Lucca and Piombino dossier records the same year as a gain.

region.text: the duchy restored to Maria Beatrice

ledger.note: 30 May 1814: French rule ends and the duchy returns to Maria Beatrice (infobox 'French rule: 10 May 1796-30 May 1814'; 'The Congress again assigned to Maria Beatrice the ancestral duchy'). The page does not narrate the restoration or give the Congress year. The Lucca and Piombino dossier routes its 1814 loss of this land to the Austrian Empire.

region.text: the imperial fiefs in Lunigiana, 'not reconstituted by the Congress of Vienna and bestowed upon her'

ledger.note: 1815: Maria Beatrice receives the Lunigiana fiefs. The Modena page says the former imperial fiefs in Lunigiana were 'not reconstituted by the Congress of Vienna and bestowed upon her'; the duchy page says they began with the Marquisate of Fosdinovo. Neither lists the fiefs, so the whole of Lunigiana is the nearest name (as in the Modena dossier); neither dates her receipt within 1815 (it precedes the December transfer).

region.text: the former imperial fiefs in Lunigiana

ledger.note: December 1815: Francis IV takes the Lunigiana fiefs. 'In December 1815 he obtained the transfer from his mother Maria Beatrice d'Este of the former imperial fiefs in Lunigiana'.

region.text: the Duchy of Massa and the Principality of Carrara

ledger.note: 1829: Modena inherits Massa and Carrara. 'In 1829, on the death of Maria Beatrice, the Duchy of Massa and the Principality of Carrara were annexed' by her son Francis IV; the Modena page: 'On her death in 1829, he also inherited the Duchy of Massa and Carrara'. The formal annexation date in the infobox is 14 November 1836.

region.text: the Duchy of Massa and the Principality of Carrara

ledger.note: 1829: the last Cybo-Malaspina state ends. 'Many authors argue that the final year of the states of Massa and Carrara was 1829'; it 'was legally transformed into a district of the duchy only in 1836'.

wars.name: French conquest of 1796
wars.outcome: 'In 1796 the Este were deprived of their possessions by the troops of Napoleon', who incorporated the land into the Cispadane Republic; French rule lasted from 10 May 1796 to 30 May 1814.
wars.note: The page names no battle or campaign; the war is listed so the reviewer can see it was considered.

certainty.note: A small feudal state whose frontier with Lucca, Tuscany and Modena is not described on the pages; the French years 1796-1814 are not the duchy's.
Sharp from the Congress of Vienna settlement and the December 1815 transfer of the Lunigiana fiefs; the pages give no survey line, so the Lunigiana fiefs stay soft as a region.

notes: No Cliopatria row: every keyframe is new. Start 1473 follows the duchy page's own statement that the state's nucleus was born on 22 February 1473; the infobox 'Established' is 22 February 1664 (the duchy title) and its predecessors are the Principality of Massa and the Marquisate of Carrara, which have no dossiers: the dossier treats Lordship, Marquisate, Principality and Duchy as renames of one state, and a gap-filler could split it at 1664. The page does not say who sold Carrara in 1473 or who held Massa before. The French years 1796-1814 are drawn as a loss to the Cispadane Republic and a gain back in 1814; the pages do not say which French-controlled state held the land in 1797-1805 (the Cisalpine and Italian Republics and the Kingdom of Italy are possible; the Kingdom of Italy of 1805-1814 has no dossier). The Lucca and Piombino dossier records a 1814 loss of Massa-Carrara to the Austrian Empire, not to this duchy. The Lunigiana region stands for fiefs no page lists; Garfagnana (Este land annexed to Lucca in 1806) is not on either page. The Cliopatria row 'Grand Duchy of Tuscany' 1797-1847 (before its 1848 shape) is a 1,032 km2 shape of three cells (bbox 9.97-10.54E, 43.86-44.19N) that overlaps both the Massa and Carrara circles (2 cells) and Lucca province (2 cells): a small mislabelled row, for the Lucca and Massa gap-fillers to settle.
